_note: Pros/cons written by Claude from the pooled Myntra review text captured in raw_reviews_<run>.json for the same run. Every point is grounded in what reviewers actually wrote; no external LLM API is involved.

top_pros: Lightweight build is the single most repeated compliment — buyers wear them for gym, road runs and full days on their feet without fatigue
Cushioning is described as responsive rather than mushy, giving noticeable energy return on road runs
True to size and comfortable straight out of the box, with no break-in period needed
Premium finish (leather and mesh uppers) means the same pair works for training and casual wear
Breathable uppers that stay cool, and on the ASICS dry quickly after wet runs
top_cons: Packaging arrives damaged or poor even when buyers are happy with the shoe itself
The ASICS Noosa Tri 16 is a specialist fast-run shoe — reviewers say it resists slow jogging and pushes you forward
Recurring anxiety about authenticity when buying premium brands online
focal_pros: The Softride/SoftFoam+ ride is described as genuinely bouncy, and repeat buyers rate it more comfortable than the Skechers Arch Fit they switched from
Strong arch support — reviewers report 8+ hours on their feet without fatigue
Light enough to help rather than hinder during cardio and running
Trendy styling at a price buyers consider a bargain
focal_cons: The midsole is judged too soft, putting extra pressure on the legs over long walks or runs
Unusual vertical creasing across the toe box, which buyers flag as unlike the horizontal creasing they expect
Reviewers position it for walking, casual wear and light jogging — explicitly not for intense running or high-performance training, with breathability called out as a weak point

top_pros: Traction on outdoor Indian cement courts is the standout strength, called excellent by multiple reviewers
High and mid-top silhouettes deliver real ankle support for court play
Priced far below Nike and Adidas, and widely seen as strong value for beginners and intermediate players
Breathable mesh keeps feet cool, and the shoes are comfortable enough to wear casually all day
Durability can be excellent — one HRX buyer reports 1.5 years of hard use still holding up
top_cons: A severe durability failure on the Red Tape pair: lace straps broke within two practice sessions, the shoe tore at the ankle and yellowed at the toe
Cushioning is below average for genuine basketball — acceptable for beginners but not for serious play
Visible glue at the joints and inconsistent quality control, particularly on HRX
Sizing runs small — several reviewers advise ordering one size up

top_pros: Lightweight and cushioned enough to cover gym sessions, long walks, trekking and daily wear from one pair
Exceptional value — Lotto buyers say the cushioning matches shoes costing Rs 8,000-10,000
Versatile styling that reviewers pair with jeans, skirts, western outfits and office wear
The chunky sole adds height, which several buyers call out as a deliberate plus
Reliable grip and breathable mesh across all three products
top_cons: The chunky silhouette divides opinion — some find it too bulky and out of proportion with their legs
The added heel height is not to everyone's taste
White colourways mark easily and need constant care
The Lotto pair is considered a little heavy for actual running, better suited to gym and walking
Some units arrive with visible stains or marks on the upper
focal_pros: Comfortable from the first wear with no break-in time required
Very lightweight, with cushioning that holds up over long days — one reviewer confirms it after a full year of use
The clean all-white mesh upper reads as premium and sleek, working for both daily and casual wear
True to size with a fit reviewers consistently call perfect
Breathable enough for gym sessions and all-day wear
focal_cons: Sits flat — a shorter reviewer specifically wanted more heel height, which the chunky rivals in this band do provide
Praise is dominated by comfort and looks, with little evidence in the reviews of it being used for serious running

top_pros: The memory-foam and Goga Mat cushioning is described over and over as 'walking on a cloud' — it is the reason people buy
Genuine therapeutic benefit: reviewers with plantar fasciitis and heel pain report relief, and regular walkers buy them to protect their joints
Ultra-lightweight with a breathable engineered mesh upper
Arch support pitched just right — neither flat nor excessively high
Deep brand trust; many are repeat Skechers buyers who say the brand never disappoints
top_cons: Sizing runs large — multiple reviewers advise buying one size smaller than usual
Occasional cosmetic defects such as spots or marks on arrival
focal_pros: Responsive, bouncy midsole cushioning paired with grip reviewers call fantastic
Lightweight with a snug but not tight fit, and a breathable upper that stays cool through long workouts
Durable engineered upper, with reflective detailing that buyers noticed in low light
Seen as strong value, particularly when discounted
focal_cons: Positive feedback clusters around gym and indoor workouts rather than distance running
The upper is described as 'a kind of plastic engineered material', a mixed reaction next to the plush textile feel rivals are praised for

top_pros: Max-cushion and ArchFit stability win this band — buyers cite excellent arch support over long wear
The ASICS GT-2000 13 delivers credible stability technology (FF Blast+, PureGEL, 3D Guidance) that overpronators say works, holding up over roughly 250 km
The Nike Free RN's sock-like knit and slip-on convenience is genuinely loved
Lightweight yet durable, and buyers who checked authenticity at a brand outlet confirmed the products are genuine
top_cons: The Nike Free RN's narrow, tapered toe box keeps feet under constant pressure — one reviewer preferred the older RN 11 and would not repurchase
Nike's knit upper attracts dust and discolours permanently, surviving washing
Energy return on the ASICS GT-2000 13 is rated only average against rivals such as the Nike Structure 26
Price is the recurring objection at this tier, and size availability gaps force returns
